objective: Rewrite the legacy Next.js 12 and React 17 Telnyx Meet sample as a maintainable Nuxt 3 and Vue 3 application using TypeScript and the Composition API, while preserving supported meeting behavior, secure server routes, and a reproducible automated verification boundary.
expected_outcomes: The fork contains a buildable Nuxt 3 and Vue 3 application with no production React, Next.js, Grommet, or styled-components runtime.
The Telnyx Video SDK is isolated behind a typed Vue composable or adapter with deterministic lifecycle cleanup and test doubles.
The original room discovery, pre-join, meeting, media, participant, chat, invitation, diagnostics, presentation, and reconnect workflows remain available.
The room and token HTTP operations remain server-side so Telnyx credentials are never exposed to the browser.
The migration is independently tested, reviewed, integrated, benchmarked against the same-workload baseline, and reproducible from a clean checkout.
included_scope: Replace the Next.js and React application shell with Nuxt 3, Vue 3, TypeScript, and Composition API conventions
Preserve landing, room list, room lookup, room join, direct room URL, loading, error, and not-found flows
Preserve server API behavior for rooms, client token generation, client token refresh, and dial-out without exposing credentials
Create a typed Telnyx Video SDK boundary for initialization, connection state, subscriptions, participant events, streams, messages, active speaker, network metrics, and teardown
Preserve media preview, permission handling, camera and microphone toggles, input and output device selection, screen sharing, mixed audio, diagnostics, virtual backgrounds, and video rendering

Preserve participant grid and presentation layouts, participant and invitation side panels, chat, WebRTC statistics, bitrate and network metric views, optional query feature flags, notifications, and automatic reconnect
Preserve PWA metadata and existing non-secret public assets
Add deterministic unit, component, server-route, and browser smoke tests using mocked Telnyx and media boundaries
Add lint, type-check, build, and test commands suitable for clean CI
Document the architecture, environment variables, local development, testing, migration decisions, supported behavior, and known limitations
excluded_scope: Changing the public Telnyx Video SDK or its upstream repository
A product redesign unrelated to the Vue migration
Pushing commits or branches to team-telnyx/telnyx-meet
Changing main in either the fork or upstream repository
Using production credentials, production rooms, or destructive external operations
Requiring a live Telnyx call for automated acceptance
Replacing Telnyx functionality with simulated UI in production code
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout installs from its committed lockfile and passes the documented build, type-check, lint, unit, component, server-route, and browser smoke commands on the declared Node version.
Production dependencies and source contain no React, React DOM, Next.js, Grommet, React Font Awesome, React Hot Toast, React Draggable, React Resize Detector, or styled-components runtime.
Vue source uses Composition API boundaries for durable meeting state and cleans up SDK listeners, tracks, timers, object URLs, and media streams when the room or component is disposed.
Telnyx API credentials remain server-only and the browser receives only the minimum room or token data required by the existing flows.
Direct room URLs and optional feature query parameters continue to work, including supplied client and refresh tokens.
Room connect, disconnect, token refresh, reconnect, participant, stream, presentation, message, active-speaker, track, and network-metric events are covered through a deterministic typed SDK fake.

Camera, microphone, device selection, screen share, audio output, media preview, virtual background, diagnostics, chat, participant, invite, WebRTC-stat, and network-metric interactions have component or end-to-end coverage.
The responsive participant and presentation layouts render usable desktop and narrow viewport states without relying on React components.
Server-route tests cover successful and failed room listing, room lookup, join token, refresh token, and dial-out requests, including request validation and upstream error mapping.
No secret value, local environment file, model credential, room credential, or generated benchmark evidence containing secrets is tracked.
The final evidence proves all accepted writes stayed on the fork's vue-fastvm-benchmark branch and upstream and both main branches were not mutated.
The repository includes an architecture overview, behavior parity matrix, environment and security notes, clean build instructions, test instructions, and migration notes.
evidence_requirements: Clean-checkout dependency installation, build, type-check, lint, unit, component, server-route, and browser smoke logs
Static dependency and source scans proving the removed React and Next.js runtime is absent
Server-secret boundary and credential scan evidence
Telnyx SDK fake contract tests and meeting event lifecycle evidence
Responsive screenshots for landing, pre-join, connected meeting, participant panel, chat, presentation, and representative error states
Behavior parity matrix linked to tests and source paths
Candidate, decision, conflict, CI, merge, changed-line, cost, timing, and FastVM cleanup receipts
Git evidence proving all writes stayed on the fork's vue-fastvm-benchmark branch
